name: Listeria monocytogenes
short_description: Short Gram-positive rod that keeps growing at fridge temperature and lives inside host cells, where it hijacks the host's own actin to build a comet tail at one pole and rockets from cell to cell; the classic foodborne danger of pregnancy, the newborn, the elderly and the immunosuppressed.

textbook.1: accept (superseded): correct short Gram-positive rod with a two-layer envelope, no spore, a bushy pale-blue host-actin tail at one pole and gold ActA studs on that pole — but the two coral flagella spring from the SAME pole as the actin tail, which blurs exactly the distinction the figure exists to teach
textbook.2: accept (chosen): muted educational palette, thin outlines, full-bleed dusky-mauve host-cell background. Envelope shown in section as exactly TWO layers (thick sage peptidoglycan wall over a violet plasma membrane) — no outer membrane, no LPS fringe, no capsule. Irregular lobed blue-purple nucleoid and teal ribosomes in an ivory-amber cytoplasm; NO spore and no bulge anywhere. The actin comet tail is unmistakably a dense branching meshwork of many hundreds of fine pale-blue host filaments springing from ONE pole, with a gold ring of ActA studs exactly where they attach; the four coral flagella attach to the opposite half of the cell and sweep the other way, so tail and flagella can never be confused. No text, no border, no artefacts

sem.1: reject: good short gold rod and a dense fibrous polar tail, but the flagella were rendered in the same pale blue-grey as the actin filaments and merged into the tail — the single most damaging error this organism can have in a picture
sem.2: reject (near miss): flagella now false-coloured coral and clearly separate from the tail, but pale wispy strands sweep in across all four corners of the substrate and read as a soft frame/vignette around the specimen
sem.3: accept (chosen): clean, flat, evenly-lit finely-granular teal-grey substrate with nothing in the corners and no vignette. Short butter-gold coccobacillus about three times longer than wide with smoothly domed poles, uniform width, no bulge and no spore. From one pole only, a dense tangled mat of individually-resolved pale blue-white host actin filaments, criss-crossing and branching; four thin coral flagella spring from the opposite half and trail across the substrate, unmistakably a different structure. Surface only, as SEM should be. No text, no scale bar, no data band, no border

3d.1: reject: attractive branched pale-blue tail and correctly unipolar gold ActA, but the specimen sits small and offset in the frame and the coral flagella emerge from the tail pole
3d.2: reject: the tail degenerated into a bundle of long parallel strands that reads as a ponytail or paintbrush rather than a branched network, and gold ActA studs appeared at BOTH poles
3d.3: reject: composition fixed and background clean, but the gold ActA studs cluster on the pole OPPOSITE the tail — backwards — and the tail reads as a heap of loose disconnected sticks
3d.4: accept (chosen, escalated to gemini-3-pro-image): rod centred on a smooth seamless dusky-mauve ground with no vignette. Long clean cutaway along the flank shows exactly two Gram-positive envelope layers as continuous bands — a thick sage peptidoglycan wall over a thin violet plasma membrane — with an amber cytoplasm, a loose lobed blue-purple nucleoid tangle and scattered teal ribosomes; no spore, no bulge, no organelles. A dense cap of gold ActA studs sits on the tail pole and only that pole, in direct contact with the base of a connected, branching pale blue-white meshwork of host actin filaments. Four thin coral flagella spring from the opposite pole and sides. Natural biological tints throughout, not near-monochrome and not neon

watercolor.1: reject: full-bleed aged paper is right, but the nucleoid was painted inside a rounded internal pocket that reads as an endospore — the one hard-fail structure for this organism — and the specimen sits small on the sheet with the tail painted as long flowing hair rather than a bushy thicket
watercolor.2: accept (chosen): warm aged paper filling the frame corner to corner, with a soft dusky-mauve host-cytoplasm wash painted directly on it — no sheet, mat, border, margin band, deckled edge or drop shadow. Short rod with a thick sage wall over a violet membrane, ivory-amber cytoplasm, a loose lobed blue-purple nucleoid lying free in the cytoplasm (no pocket, no spore) and fine teal ribosome stipples. The actin comet tail is a short, dense, visibly branching thicket of fine ink strands over a pale blue-grey wash, unipolar; coral flagella in delicate ink linework spring from the opposite half

reference: accept: CDC PHIL #2287 (Public Domain, PD-USGov-HHS-CDC, CDC / Elizabeth White, 2002), a transmission electron micrograph of a flagellated Listeria monocytogenes bacterium at 41,250x. Native resolution is 2212 x 2767 px, verified through the Wikimedia API — genuinely high-resolution, nothing was upscaled. It unambiguously shows the organism: a single short rod roughly two and a half times longer than wide with evenly domed poles, no bulge and no spore, and two long fine flagella clearly traced against the support film. The download (real-01) is greyscale and carries no text or scale bar. real-02 is an edit_image.py false-colour pass (gemini-2.5-flash-image) and was checked side by side against real-01: the rod outline, the flagellar paths, the dust specks and the film grain are all preserved unchanged, so it is a colourisation, not a re-illustration. real-03, the DISPLAY image, is a plain deterministic PIL centre crop and LANCZOS resize of real-02 with NO model involved, done to bring the small specimen up to a legible size. TWO HONEST CAVEATS. (1) The false colour flipped the flagella from dark grey threads to pale threads against the teal background; their paths are unchanged but their tonal relationship to the background is not the original's. (2) No freely-licensed photograph or fluorescence image of the actin comet tail could be found anywhere in the public domain or under CC — comet-tail figures live only inside paywalled journal articles — so the tail in all four rendered styles is built from the literature (ActA-nucleated, Arp2/3-branched, unipolar, ~0.02-1.4 um/s) and is NOT traced from a photograph. The reference therefore documents the rod's proportions, poles and flagella only.
decision: gen-02__gemini-2.5-flash-image — the primary teaching figure and the svg_theme: the clearest statement of the two-layer Gram-positive envelope, the spore-free interior, and above all the unipolar host-actin comet tail set against oppositely-directed flagella. Base for labels.json.

gen-03__gemini-2.5-flash-image — the best silhouette in the set and the closest match to the real TEM: a short stubby rod with the tail as a matted fibrous polar thicket. Deliberately left unlabelled; SEM shows surface only and its teaching value here is the bare outline next to the real micrograph.

gen-04__gemini-3-pro-image — took four passes and an escalation to the Pro model to get ActA onto the correct pole while keeping the tail a connected branching network and the background vignette-free.
gen-02__gemini-2.5-flash-image — full-bleed paper, no spore-like pocket, and the branchiest, most obviously non-flagellar rendering of the tail in the whole set.
notes: Model ladder: all four styles started on gemini-2.5-flash-image; only 3d needed escalation to gemini-3-pro-image (attempt 4) after three bad results. Eleven science renders in total (textbook 2, sem 3, 3d 4, watercolor 2), plus one reference download, one reference colour-edit, one deterministic reference crop and one coloring page. THE TWO HARD-FAIL ITEMS WERE BOTH CAUGHT AND FIXED, not talked around: (a) NO ENDOSPORE — Listeria does not form spores, and the watercolor attempt 1 that painted the nucleoid inside a spore-like oval pocket was thrown away rather than kept; every accepted render has a plain, uniform-width cell body with no knob, bulge or internal compartment. (b) THE ACTIN TAIL IS NOT A FLAGELLUM — SEM attempt 1 was rejected purely because the flagella shared the tail's colour, and textbook attempt 1 was superseded because the flagella left the same pole as the tail. In every accepted render the tail is a dense branching meshwork of many fine filaments in a cool pale blue-white (a deliberately different colour family from every bacterial structure, marking it as HOST material), it springs from ONE pole only, and the coral flagella attach to the opposite half. KNOWN COMPROMISES, flagged honestly: (i) the accepted textbook, 3d and watercolor cells are roughly three and a half to four times longer than wide, at the long end of the documented 1-2 x 0.4-0.5 um coccobacillus range; only the sem render hits the stubby ~3:1 ideal, and the real TEM reference is stubbier still at ~2.5:1. (ii) Flagella are drawn on all four styles for teaching completeness even though the intracellular, 37 C state actually shown here is the one in which MogR represses flagellar expression — the honest reading is 'this is what the cell has, not what it would be expressing at that instant'; the label text carries the '(only below ~30 C)' caveat in the research file and the temperature rule is stated in the descriptions. (iii) The ruptured phagosome remnant and VASP/profilin at the growing tail tip are described in the science section but are not drawn or labelled — at this scale neither separates reliably in the generated art. (iv) The host-cell context is carried only by a dim mauve background with a few blurred out-of-focus organelle shapes; the style rules require an uncluttered background for label legibility, so no explicit host membrane, nucleus or neighbouring cell is shown. (v) The Arp2/3 branch junctions are visible as Y-branches in the artwork but are folded into the 'host actin filaments' label rather than given their own leader line.
